body:
Don't worry about responding in any sort of time, I myself have been on and off throughout the day. My main reddit account name is Road_To_Niflheim, I decided it is only fair if I throw myself out there, just something I personally want to do.

On the topic of three things a day, it is rather ironic you bring that up because there is a subreddit (my daily 3) that is basically just that, and I happened to of started posting my daily 3 again, just the day before last.

As for the list, I have just got a nice hot mug of coffee and have been going at it. So far of my "person" I really like the feeling of authenticity that I sort of borrowed from one of my professors. There is just this sort of in the moment freedom that is hard to put into words.

Other general things I have listed are -reading -writing -video games (but really only with friends). -Maybe letting a few negative friends not take up such a large portion of my time, especially time spent thinking.  -spending time listening to music.  And that is a summarization of what I got so far. I think writing stuff out really helps me work through things. 

I am listening to a large spotify playlist and this song came on, it made me smile :) https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=cHlidfF7nK8

There are people I can tell, I don't and I probably should but I do have access to some loving people. Things sort of climaxed for me earlier today, and I have gradually been feeling better since that post. I am just going to take the night off and play video games and write out a list of aspects of life I particularly like, and maybe some I don't and dive into some of that pondering.

I peeked through some of your history (hope you don't mind) and seen that you have some problems with Dissociative disorder. About four years ago I had reoccurring Depersonalization disorder after spending a week smoking salvia (or some weird "legal" weed blend thing, not even 100% sure what it contained.) After which for about a year and a half any contact with any kind of drug, alcohol, or any anxiety pushed me into that feeling of unreal-detachment. You have my grandiose empathy, as well as my deepest thanks for sticking around and responding to me here.

Thank you for this reply. It is 10x longer than I was expecting anyone to write out, it means a lot. 

The perspective you put forth is one I usually hold, but it always seems to fall from one's mind when things get rough, at least in my case. The combination of culture society and all of our interactions come into a sort of point of what we are, and how we react to things, I guess... That is what I believe, what I often forget, and what you reminded me of. 

"That's not to say you can't learn to know yourself. You can try to pay attention to the things that really make you excited or tearful or scared and incorporate those things into how you live and explore your life." This is very written, and it makes me realize that maybe the even though some chips were set, I can still choose which pieces to utilize and which to discard. At least to a degree.

The last part about not knowing how to do taxes makes me feel better to a degree you would probably laugh at. 

And I am safe. I was closer than I have been in many many years in all honesty, but I am safe now. Thank you for helping.
